Teacher Eyes Only

Solutions for Level B: Inheritance.

Concept Overview

  • Inheritance: Creating specialised versions (`class Brute(Player)`) of a base class.
  • Super: Calling the parent constructor (`super().__init__`) to set up basic stats before customising.
  • Polymorphism (Preview): Treating Butes and Scouts as "Players".

Common Misconceptions

1. Forgetting `super().__init__(name)`

If they don't call super, `self.name` and other base stats won't be set, causing crashes. It's crucial to "build the parent first".

2. Redefining methods unnecessarily

Students might copy-paste `take_damage` into Brute. Explain that they inherit it for free!

Solution Code

from .player import Player

class Brute(Player):
    """Start with high HP, low accuracy."""
    def __init__(self, name):
        super().__init__(name)  # CRITICAL
        self.health = 120
        self.max_health = 120   # Must match
        self.armour = 3
        self.accuracy = 70

    def describe_specialty(self):
        return "Brute: Tanky but clumsy."


class Scout(Player):
    """Start with low HP, high accuracy."""
    def __init__(self, name):
        super().__init__(name)  # CRITICAL
        self.health = 80
        self.max_health = 80
        self.armour = 1
        self.accuracy = 95

    def describe_specialty(self):
        return "Scout: Agile glass cannon."
